competency_fulfillment.rationale: Ordering tasks like '13, 1, 14 -> 1, 13, 14' correctly test smallest-to-largest sequencing, but the range explored is much narrower than the stated 'up to 100' ceiling.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Values across seeds 42-46 span only 1 to 14; no sample shows two-digit numbers in the 20-99 band that the competency's 'up to 100' wording implies should be tested.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The ordering instruction and three-item lists are appropriately concrete and readable for Grade 1 Q2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three-number lists with mixed single- and double-digit values (e.g. 12, 5, 10) show the format can mix digit lengths, a good structural variant.

competency_alignment.rationale: All samples are genuine ascending-order tasks, matching 'Order numbers up to 100 from smallest to largest' in structure.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The highest number across all 5 samples is 14, well under a fifth of the stated 100 ceiling, so the extended range this node is meant to add over the Grade 1 Q1 node is not evidenced.
